title: Rack slot utilization and cold-aisle contingency plan
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a pragmatic approach to maximizing GPU rack slot utilization while keeping cold-aisle thermal and power risk low for small-to-medium on-prem and colocation pods. It is intended for infra leads, site ops, and the SRE-run deployment crew who will stage GPU pods into racks and coordinate with colocation facilities.

Scope:
- Applies to single-datahall GPU pods (4–20 racks) and mid-size colo cages where cold-aisle containment is partial or variable.
- Focus areas: slot population plan, per-rack power & breaker allocation, CRAC interaction, thermal thresholds, deployment phasing, and contingency actions for thermal/power excursions.
- Not covering network fabric design, UPS sizing beyond immediate rack PDU headroom, or full datahall power engineering reports.

Executive summary:
- Target utilization: 70% sustained average slot population per pod to preserve 25% thermal/power headroom for transient spikes and future scaling.
- Default per-rack planning envelope: 18kW steady-state budget with 22kW breaker provisioning (20% transient margin).
- Cold aisle policy: aim for containment or focused air curtains at racks with >12kW sustained draw. If containment not possible, cap per-rack sustained power at 14kW and stagger population.
- Deployment stance: stage-by-stage (smoke -> soak -> ramp) with thermal telemetry gating at each stage.

Assumptions and baseline inputs:
- Typical accelerator example: NVIDIA A100 80GB (250–450 W idle-to-peak under inference workloads); denote 3.5–4.5 kW per 4-GPU tray depending on power profile/voltages.
- Fans, servers, and auxiliary gear add 10–15% overhead to card TDP.
- Floor-level CRAC delta-T target: 12–16C at cold-aisle intake. Hot-aisle should be managed to avoid >45C return to CRAC.
- We assume single PDU per rack with 2x basic PDUs (for dual feed, but not automatic transfer) and local breaker rating of 63A @ 208V where available.

Per-rack power and slot allocation guidance:
- Rack class A (high-density, contained): up to 20kW steady-state, up to 24x 3.0–3.5 kW equivalent slots (use validated trays). Require cold-aisle containment and dedicated CRAC zoning.
- Rack class B (partial containment / mixed): target 12–18kW steady-state. Limit full-power trays so sustained per-slot average <=3.0 kW.
- Rack class C (no containment / legacy aisles): cap at 10–14kW steady-state. Distribute heavy trays across multiple racks to avoid aisle hot spots.
- Always reserve 20–25% headroom on breaker capacity to avoid nuisance trips and to allow maintenance.

Thermal monitoring and gating thresholds (telemetry required):
- Cold-aisle intake temp rise >3C within 30 minutes -> hold new slot populations until investigation.
- Intake temp >30C -> immediate reduction of incoming workload (shift to canary region or throttle).
- CRAC return air >45C at any time -> engage emergency throttle, schedule PV test, and notify facility.
- Rack-level PDU current >85% sustained for >10 minutes -> trigger placement hold and notify SRE.

Deployment phasing checklist (detailed):
1) Pre-stage (week -1 to 0): verify rack mechanical fit, airflow baffles in place, PDU commissioning complete, KVM/IPMI baseline tests, and power metering hooked to telemetry.
2) Smoke (day 0): install 1 tray or single GPU server per rack, verify power draw, IPMI, temp sensors, and logging to telemetry. Hold for 4 hours.
3) Soak (day 1–2): ramp to 30% of planned final population; run synthetic loads representative of inference (batch sizes and sequence lengths usual for hosted usage) for 24 hours. Verify stability, CRAC response.
4) Ramp (day 3–7): step to 60% then 90% with 24–48 hour observation windows. Only proceed if thermal and PDU metrics remain within thresholds.
5) Final cutover: enable production traffic and monitor closely for 72 hours.

Contingency actions (ordered):
- Minor intake drift: reduce software frequency scaling (throttle GPUs to power cap), shift lower-priority jobs to other regions.
- PDU high current alarm: pause new boot cycles, reduce per-machine power caps to free headroom, coordinate with colo on breaker trip risk.
- CRAC insufficient response: activate portable HVAC (short-term), redistribute heavy servers to racks closer to CRAC return, and defer additional population.
- Persistent hot-aisle issue: migrate heavy workloads out, deploy temporary containment walls, and schedule vendor HVAC remediation.

Slot-level population heuristics (practical rules):
- Mix heavy trays with 1–2 light-density mgmt servers per rack to distribute I/O and fan heat.
- Avoid clumping all heavy trays in adjacent racks in same aisle without containment.
- Prefer alternating heavy/light across front-to-back to create uniform intake temp profile.

Capacity example (worked):
Pod target: 10 racks, planned GPU trays: 80 trays (8 per rack average)
- If designing for 18kW/rack steady => planned capacity used = 10 racks * 18 kW = 180 kW steady
- Headroom target 25% => usable planned load = 135 kW => average per-tray budget = 135 kW / 80 = 1.6875 kW/tray (conservative inference profile)
- If chosen trays are 3.5 kW peak, need to reduce active concurrency or proportion of hot trays per rack to hit steady goal. This is why staging + throttling is required.

Risk register (top entries):
- Facility power derating during summer (likelihood: medium; impact: high) -> mitigation: reserve extra breaker capacity in rollout plan and ability to offload traffic to hosted region.
- Inaccurate per-server power models (likelihood: high; impact: medium) -> mitigation: early measurement in smoke phase and update inventory power model.
- Cold-aisle mixing due to under-specified containment (likelihood: medium; impact: high) -> mitigation: deploy temporary curtains and strict slot staggering.

Operational runbooks (short pointers):
- Thermal-excursion runbook ID: INF-TR-09 (link in Confluence). Steps include automated power caps, paged on-call, facility notification, and staged rollback.
- PDU trip runbook ID: INF-PDU-04.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Colo contract allowance for temporary portable AC units? (Ops to confirm with procurement)
- Default per-tray power cap to apply in no-containment racks (recommend 2.5 kW until measured).
- Telemetry sampling cadence – propose 30s telemetry for PDU currents and 1m for temperature.

Next steps and owners:
- Aisha: finalize per-tray power models with Applied ML (due 2026-02-18).
- Ethan: update telemetry dashboards and gating alarms (due 2026-02-12).
- Laura: confirm colo contract for portable HVAC and additional CRAC scheduling (due 2026-02-20).
- Miguel: run pilot stage at West-2 pod next week and populate results in Confluence.

Appendix: quick checklist for on-site techs:
- Verify blanking panels installed and cable management does not obstruct airflow.
- Confirm PDU load balancing across phases per vendor guidance.
- Ensure temperature sensors present at top/bottom of cold aisle every 3 racks.
- Tag any fan-failure or anomalous return logs and escalate immediately.

Notes to self: this is intentionally prescriptive but conservative — aim to update after two pod rollouts and remove overly conservative caps where telemetry supports it.
